section_summary.extract_value: This section outlines the objectives and hypotheses of a study examining college women's body image and eating behaviors in relation to exposure to body-focused and non-body-focused others. The study employs a multi-level design examining effects at between-persons (average exposure over a week), within-persons (day-to-day variations), and temporal (day-to-day changes) levels. The hypotheses predict that greater exposure to non-body-focused others will be associated with better body image and more intuitive eating, while greater exposure to body-focused others will be associated with worse body image and more restrained eating.
